Week 62 Appendix: The Clock Holds, Barely, Under War

A week of unauthorized war escalation, ballot seizures, and airport dragnets tested a democracy already worn thin, without moving the needle.

This was a week in which an undeclared, escalating war with Iran collided with domestic institutional breakdown, producing compounding pressure across nearly every category of democratic decay. Trump publicly celebrated Robert Mueller's death, called Democrats America's 'greatest enemy,' and threatened war crimes against Iranian civilian infrastructure, all while acknowledging he was avoiding the word 'war' to evade constitutional authorization requirements. Simultaneously, ICE agents were deployed to airports amid a DHS shutdown Bannon called a 'test run' for the midterms, a California sheriff seized 650,000 ballots on baseless fraud claims, and Trump demanded the SAVE America Act and filibuster elimination as conditions for funding government. Reporting also surfaced serious corruption threads—Kushner's Saudi payments amid Iran war advice, Lewandowski's alleged pay-for-contracts scheme, and possible insider trading on presidential war announcements. Republican officials in Congress and the military (Mace, Rogers, Kent) showed rare cracks in loyalty, while courts delivered mixed but meaningful checks.

Power and Authority

  1. Trump threatened to deploy ICE agents to airports and demanded voting restrictions as a condition for DHS funding: The president threatened to deploy federal immigration agents to airports and tied government funding to sweeping voting restrictions, coercing legislative outcomes with executive force. (2026-03-21)
  2. Trump deployed ICE agents to airports nationwide, including tactical-gear personnel with no clear operational plan: Immigration enforcement agents replaced airport security screeners with no defined mission, blurring lines between civilian security and federal immigration power. (2026-03-22)
  3. Trump declared the Democratic Party America's greatest enemy: A sitting president labeled a major domestic political party the nation's greatest enemy, escalating divisive rhetoric during an active foreign war. (2026-03-22) [single source]
  4. Trump threatened to bomb Iranian civilian power plants and issued a 48-hour ultimatum: The president publicly threatened to destroy civilian energy infrastructure, an act international law experts said would constitute a war crime, escalating conflict without congressional authorization. (2026-03-22)
  5. Trump defended $200 billion military funding request despite claiming the Iran war was ending: The president suggested continued massive military spending was needed regardless of claimed diplomatic progress, raising questions about the true purpose of war funding. (2026-03-23)
  6. Trump attacked Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico while withholding endorsement in the Texas GOP primary: The president used his platform to attack a political opponent while remaining publicly uncommitted in his own party's primary, reflecting personal grievance over party strategy. (2026-03-22)
  7. Trump acknowledged deliberately avoiding the word "war" to circumvent constitutional authorization requirements: The president admitted at a fundraiser that he used alternate terminology specifically to sidestep the constitutional requirement for congressional approval of war. (2026-03-26) [single source]
  8. Trump signed executive order to unilaterally pay TSA workers during a government shutdown: The president invoked emergency powers to direct payment of federal workers, bypassing Congress's constitutional control over appropriations. (2026-03-27)
  9. Trump demanded Senate eliminate the filibuster and add all SAVE America Act provisions to funding legislation: The president pressed for removal of a core Senate minority-rights protection to force passage of restrictive voting measures, undermining legislative checks on majority power. (2026-03-27)
  10. Trump posted celebratory and derogatory messages about the death of former FBI Director Robert Mueller: A sitting president publicly celebrated a deceased former investigator's death, degrading norms of civility and respect toward institutional oversight figures. (2026-03-21)
  11. Trump endorsed Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán for reelection: The president publicly backed a foreign authoritarian-leaning leader ahead of an election, signaling U.S. alignment with anti-democratic governance abroad. (2026-03-26)
  12. Treasury Department removed the treasurer's signature and added Trump's own signature to U.S. paper currency: For the first time in 165 years, a sitting president's personal signature will appear on legal tender, blending presidential power with personal branding of a public institution. (2026-03-27) [single source]
